definition: Multimodal Large Language Model — an LLM extended to consume images (and often audio/video) alongside text, e.g. GPT-4V and LLaVA.
details: Multimodal Large Language Model — an LLM extended to consume images (and often audio/video) alongside text, e.g. GPT-4V and LLaVA.

explainer.lead: An MLLM is a multimodal large language model: an LLM extended to consume images, and often audio or video, alongside text. It matters because it lets one model answer questions about mixed media rather than text alone.

tiers.eli5: A normal chatbot only reads words; this kind of model can look at a picture you show it and talk about what it sees.
tiers.practitioner: Examples include GPT-4V and LLaVA, so engineers use them for tasks that mix media with text prompts. The pitfall implied by the name is scope creep: not every multimodal model handles audio and video, only images and sometimes those extra formats.
tiers.paperLevel: A Multimodal Large Language Model: a large language model whose inputs are extended beyond text to include images and often audio or video. Named examples: GPT-4V and LLaVA.

explainer.example: A user uploads a photo of a receipt and asks the model over text to list the purchases, since the image and the question are handled together.
